verdict.headline: Chip stocks lead a rebound after Anthropic files for its IPO, two days before big tech reports
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 +0.70% to 7,676.77, Nasdaq +0.82% to 26,169.38, Dow +0.28%; SOXX +2.85%; VIX 18.49; 10Y 4.986%; EWZ -19.8%; Brent ~$111-116; BTC $80,241.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Anthropic publicly filed for a Nasdaq IPO under the ticker ANT, and the AI trade had its first good day in a week. The S&P 500 rose 0.70% and the Nasdaq 0.82%, while the semiconductor fund gained 2.85%, led by Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom. The 10-year held under 5% at 4.986% and the VIX fell to 18.49. Separately, Brazil's Ibovespa fell 13.88%, its worst day since March 2020, after Lula's re-election.

What it means: the filing shows $16.3 billion of first-half revenue and puts a public price on a frontier AI lab, which opens equity markets as a funding source for the biggest buyers of compute a day after Elon Musk warned that debt funding for AI data-center companies has nearly shut. The same filing shows an $80.7 billion first-half loss, mostly non-cash, and about a quarter of revenue from two customers, and the Fed still has a December hike priced at about 79%.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close above 26,424.82 after Microsoft and Alphabet report on Wednesday would show October's tech selling ending; a close back under Friday's 25,955 would show today as a one-day bounce. A 10-year above 5.11% after Wednesday's Fed decision would put rates back in charge of tech.
verdict.lede_short: Anthropic's IPO filing lifted chip stocks nearly 3% and the Nasdaq 0.82%, the AI trade's first good day in a week. The filing shows revenue growing fast enough to fund large compute purchases, but also an $80.7 billion first-half loss, and the Nasdaq is still below last week's 26,424.82. Microsoft and Alphabet on Wednesday, after the Fed, decide whether that level is cleared or today was a bounce.

supporting_data.label: Anthropic filed its S-1 to list on the Nasdaq as ANT, showing $16.3 billion of first-half revenue against an $80.7 billion mostly non-cash loss — the first public price for a frontier AI lab, with about 25% of revenue from two customers.

Nvidia rose 2.4%, AMD 2.8%, Micron 3% and Broadcom 2.3% as the semiconductor fund gained nearly 3% — the compute suppliers rose about four times as much as the S&P 500's 0.70%, so the filing was read as demand for chips.

Fed funds futures put a hold on Wednesday at about 90% and a December hike at about 79%, with the 10-year closing at 4.986% — the rate backdrop that drove October's tech selling is unchanged going into the decision.
Brazil's Ibovespa fell 13.88% and the Brazil ETF 19.8% after Lula won 51.79% of the runoff — the worst day since March 2020, after markets had priced his win at about 20%.
Brent eased on Iran diplomacy but CNBC put its settlement at $115.81, down only 0.8% — the morning's drop toward $110 largely reversed, leaving Friday's $116.72 high within reach.
Tesla rose 5.21% to its highest since July after Barclays upgraded it to overweight with a $450 target — the stock is still down about 13.7% for the year.

trade_setups.thesis: Anthropic's filing lifted chips and the Nasdaq, recovering a little under half the gap to last week's 26,424.82, with Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon spending plans due this week.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 26,424.82 would show October's tech selling ending; a capex cut or a close under 25,955 would mark today as a bounce.

trade_setups.thesis: The 10-year holds under 5% into a Fed decision where a hold is priced and the December hike odds of about 79% are the open question.
trade_setups.invalidation: A statement tying further hikes to oil would test 5.11%; pushback on December would likely take the 10-year below 4.95%.

trade_setups.thesis: Iran diplomacy eased oil intraday, but the reported settlement near $115.81 leaves Friday's six-month high close while Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue.
trade_setups.entry: $116.72 Friday settlement above; the $110 area below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above $116.72 would put oil back in charge of rates; a confirmed Iran framework would likely test $110.
